full_judgment:
This Rule calls in question the legality and propriety of the order dated 22.9.83 passed by the learned District Judge, Rangpur in Civil Revision Case No. 42 of 1983 setting aside the order dated 21.3.83 passed by the learned Munsif, 2nd Court, Gaibandha in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 50 of 1978. 

 Petitioner's predecessor-in-interest Khejer Uddin Sarkar sold the disputed agricultural land measuring 37 decimal to the principal opposite party by registered Kabala dated 2.8.74 for consideration of Taka 3,000/- on account of his economic distress. Khejer Uddin Sarkar died leaving petitioners as his legal heirs. Subsequently Ordinance No, XXVIII of 1976 was promulgated on 29.4.76, making provision for restoration of the agricultural land transferred for reasons of economic distress and petitioners preferred an application before the Circle Officer (Revenue) Fulchari for restoration of the said land under the provision of said Ordinance. The application was registered as Misc. Case No. 368 of 1976. 

 4. Mr. Azizul Huque, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the lower appellate Court committed an error in law apparent on the face of the record in computing the period of limitation inasmuch as the learned appellate Court wrongly held that the application for restoration of the land was made before the Circle Officer (Revenue) on 31.7.78 but in fact such application was filed on 29.9.76 as it is evident from fact that the application for restoration of land was registered as Misc. Case No. 368 of 1976. Since the application was registered as Misc. Case No. 368 of 1976 and as such application cannot be filed on 13.7.78 as observed by, the lower revisional Court. The learned Advocate further urged that Ordinance No. XXVIII of 1976 came into force on 27.4.74 and not on 29.4.76 as observed by the learned District Judge in his impugned order. It is under the circumstances the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the application for restoration of the land transferred was made within six months from the promulgation of the Ordinance. 

 7. I have been taken through the judgment pronounced by the learned District Judge as well as other materials on record. Admittedly the land transferred is an agricultural one and this transfer took place during the period of economic distress which commenced from the year, 1974 and ended on 31st December, 1974. There is no material on record to prove that transferor Khejer Uddin Sarkar owned more than 3 acres of land when he transferred the land in question. In fact Ordinance XXVIII of 1976 created the right of reconveyance in favour of transferor within the specified time and this right of re-conveyance is based on agreement which came into existence by fiction of law. In other words the said ordinance created the right of reconveyance which is based on agreement. Further the said Ordinance provides procedure for enforcement of that right. It is well settled that a right of reconveyance cannot be assignable unless terms of the contract manifestly restrict the right to the transferor alone. In the instant case there is no material to show that right of reconveyance is restricted to the transferor. This view received support from the case of Shaukat Ali and others reported in 27 DLR (AD) (1975) 59. It was a case of specific performance of contract for conveyance of the suit land. Their Lordships of the Appellate Division having reviewed large number of cases held that right of rcconvcyance is a transferable and heritable right. Therefore, though aforesaid Ordinance is silent on the point of heritability of the right of reconveyance it is manifest from preamble of the Ordinance that the land transferred should go back to the family of the transferor. 

 8. In fact the right conferred on the transferor under the provision of the Ordinance for being restored to the possession of the land transferred is assignable as well as heritable and as such petitioner being a sole heir of the transferor Khejer Uddin Sarkar is competent to file this application seeking the restoration of possession of the land transferred. This aspect of this case was not considered by the learned District Judge. In view of this fact the impugned order is not sustainable in law and it is accordingly set aside and that of the order dated 21.3.83 passed by the learned Munsif, 2nd Court, Gaibandha in Misc. Appeal No. 50 of 1978 is restored.
